title: Reading the Field
logline: Across one growing season, a farmer in a tank-irrigated village makes dozens of small calls, when to flood, when to weed, when to hold water back, none of them written down, all of them adding up to a harvest.

object.note: Object 10 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: Knowing by feel moves from the wheel to a whole season of water and paddy: a farmer's many unwritten calls that add up to a harvest.

thread_out.thread: From knowing without stopping to think to a single act of letting go: a stream with no bridge, a rope tied to a tree, and the moment of standing firm on the far side.

requirements: A farming household willing to be followed across a full season
Access to the field and irrigation system
Patience for a long shooting schedule tied to the crop calendar

lesson.in_simple_terms: One kind of wisdom is very practical: seeing what makes good things grow, what makes them decline, and knowing on the spot what to do. The texts say clear seeing like this grows on the ground of honest conduct and a steady mind.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: ප්‍රඥාවේ එක් පැත්තක් ඉතා ප්‍රායෝගිකයි: යමක් වැඩෙන්නේ කුමකින්ද, පිරිහෙන්නේ කුමකින්ද යන්න දැක, ඒ මොහොතේම කළ යුත්ත දැනගැනීමයි.
lesson.the_teaching: Among the kinds of wisdom (paññā) the texts list skill in growth, skill in decline and skill in means (āya, apāya and upāya kosalla): knowing how to keep harmful states from arising and let good ones grow, knowing how things fall away, and knowing in the moment what brings about wellbeing. They also set insight in an order: purification of conduct and purification of mind are its roots, and the remaining five of the seven purifications (satta visuddhi) are its body. The Margaya calls conduct and a settled mind the ground on which insight is built.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: Across one season the farmer walks the bunds at dawn, reads water levels and plant colour, and makes quick calls after sudden rain or a pest sighting, none of them written down. Talk with neighbours about last season's mistakes, and the harvest itself, let the viewer see knowing that has turned into action. The film offers this as a parallel in the fields, not a claim about the farmer's inner life.

key_terms.en: skill in growth / in decline / in means
purification; seven stages from conduct to knowledge-and-vision

lesson.caution: This is not insight in the business or self-help sense of a clever idea; in the texts insight is an undistorted seeing of how all things arise, pass and are not a self, aimed at release.
lesson.builds_on: The potter knew by feel how far the clay could go; this film widens knowing-by-feel into the practical wisdom the texts describe, which rests on conduct and a steady mind.
lesson.evidence_class: editorial interpretation grounded in cited source teaching
